title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 24 of the 4th draft of the 'Analysis situs' chapter (archive no. 33; the header digit is corrected to 24). It continues the axiomatisation of what the next page calls 'magasins' (stores of figures). A magasin is a set M of 'figures' with three primitive relations: X ≤ Y (inclusion), X <<° Y (X lies in the interior of Y), and X |◦| Y (the interiors of X and Y do not overlap). Its 'points' form the subset L of minimal elements. In the strictly divisible case of p.23 there is also a symmetric, irreflexive relation || ('separated') on L.

(1) Quasi-set-theoretic case. Here x || y is simply x ≠ y. So the data reduce to (M, ≤, <<°), and the third relation becomes derived. The left margin says that X |◦| Y can be expressed through <<°: X |◦| Y ⟺ omb°(X) ∩ omb°(Y) = ∅, where omb°(Z) = {x ∈ L | x <<° Z} is the set of interior points of Z. The axioms are:
- Mag quas 1: ≤ and <<° are orders.
- Mag quas 2: same as Mag 2' on p.21.
- Mag quas 3: every X has an interior point, i.e. there is x ∈ L with x <<° X. This is the condition Mag L1 (omb(X)° ≠ ∅) used on p.25.

(2) Set-theoretic magasins. Grothendieck remarks that these are 'the only ones people have worked on so far!'. Their structure is that of p.9, with ≤ and << induced from the set structure of Fig(L) (figures as subsets of a point set L). The relation is X |◦| Y ⟺ X° ∩ Y° = ∅, with X° = X \ ∂X the usual interior.

(3) An index of all axiom packages so far, each leading to a type of magasin:
- Mag 1-4 (p.22) with Mag L1, L2: the basic notion of magasin.
- At 1-5 (p.11-12) + Mag 1-4: atomic.
- AtM 1-5 (p.13-14) + Mag 1-4: mixed.
- Mag div 1-3 (p.23), combined with Mag 1-4 and L2: divisible.
- Mag quas 1-3: quasi-set-theoretic.
- Mag ens 1-2 (p.9): set-theoretic.
- A polyhedral variant, Mag 1-4 + Mag pol (+ Mag at pol), on pp.15-19; see also Mag 1', Mag 2' on pp.30-31.

Purpose: to give an intrinsic, possibly point-free, axiomatic foundation for 'figures' in a tame-topology programme. The set-based model is to be one special case among several (atomic, divisible, polyhedral).
errors: Mag quas 3 reads '∃ x ∈ L, avec x <<° M'; it should be x <<° X (slip of the pen).

Taken literally, Mag div 3 as transcribed on p.23 (X ≤ Y, X ≠ Y, x <<° X, y <<° Y ⇒ x || y) combined with the quasi-set reading x || y ⟺ x ≠ y would fail in set models: an interior point of X is also interior to Y. So either the p.23 axiom is mistranscribed (probably |◦| rather than ≤) or it is a draft slip. On this page itself the quasi-set and set-theoretic statements are consistent.

ideas.what: Abstract 'magasin' of figures with primitive relations inclusion ≤, interior inclusion <<°, interior-disjointness |◦|, and points defined as minimal elements.
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / region-based theory of space (part-of, non-tangential proper part, disjointness); contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Laguna 1922, Whitehead 1929, Clarke 1981, Randell–Cui–Cohn (RCC) 1992, Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras 2000s
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for an axiomatic 'tame topology' in Esquisse d'un programme §5; magasins themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Disjointness of interiors expressed via the shadow of interior points: X|◦|Y ⟺ omb°(X)∩omb°(Y)=∅.
ideas.modern_name: Representation of regions by sets of interior points (point-based models of mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in representation theorems for contact algebras (e.g. Dimov–Vakarelov)

ideas.what: Classification of magasin types: atomic, mixed, divisible, quasi-set-theoretic, set-theoretic, polyhedral.
ideas.modern_name: Atomic vs atomless (gunky) mereotopologies; polyhedral / o-minimal models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereology literature (atomistic vs atomless), PL topology

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'magasins' are essentially a mereotopology, independently reinvented. The primitives part-of, non-tangential-part and non-overlap match RCC/Clarke-style region calculi, and the set-based models with interior X\∂X match the standard topological models. His remark that set-based models are the only ones studied shows he was unaware of the point-free tradition (Whitehead, Tarski's geometry of solids, Clarke). The later literature has not linked his tame-topology programme to mereotopology or contact algebras.
missed.quote: les magasins ensemblistes (les seuls sur lesquels les gens aient travaillé jusqu'à maintenant!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Contact-algebra representation theorems could answer his implicit question of which magasins are set-theoretic. Conversely, his atomic/divisible/polyhedral classification and figure-based viewpoint might supply tame (o-minimal/PL) models for qualitative spatial reasoning.

missed.claim: The page indexes several non-equivalent axiom systems but does not prove a representation theorem saying when a quasi-set-theoretic or divisible magasin comes from a set-theoretic one, Fig(L) with interiors.
missed.quote: sont réduits à la structure de la p.9 ... comme induite par les structures ensemblistes des Fig(L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such a representation result is the natural completion. It is analogous to Stone-type duality for contact algebras.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a bookkeeping page listing axiom packages. Still, it documents that Grothendieck in 1986 was building a point-free/mereotopological axiomatics of figures, believing the set-based case to be the only one studied. That is a notable unpublished thread whose link to mereotopology seems unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: Page number: the header is '24' (corrected digit), not '29/26'; it sits between pp.23 and 25.
'amb°' should be 'omb°' (ombre, the shadow), as on p.25; the margin reads roughly: X|◦|Y ⟺ omb°(X) ∩ omb°(Y) = ∅, où omb°(Z) = {x ∈ L | x <<° Z}.
The first-line insertion reads roughly 'x||y équivaut à x ≠ y', not 'c(y) ∋ x ≠ y'.
The structures are 'magasins' (as on p.25), not 'magmas': 'les magasins ensemblistes', 'pour avoir un "magasin"'.
Mag quas 3: 'x <<° M' is in the manuscript but means x <<° X.
